column2: As long as the senses are not impaired and disease does not trouble, so long should one worship Vishnu, if he desires liberation.
The moment a creature emerges from its mother's womb, death is close at hand; therefore one should be devoted to dharma.
Alas, alas, alas — this body! Knowing it to be perishable, this man still does not practise dharma.
True, true, again true, with arm raised I say it: abandoning hypocrisy, one should worship Vasudeva.
Again and again, with arm raised, I tell you what is good, Narada: Vishnu is to be worshipped with all one's being; give up envy and falsehood.
Anger is the root of mental torment; anger is the bond of samsara. Anger destroys dharma; therefore avoid it.
This birth has desire as its root; desire is the cause of sin. Desire destroys fame; therefore avoid it.
Malice is held the cause of the whole net of sorrows and the means to hells; therefore give it up too.
The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for men; therefore, joining it to the Supreme Self, be happy.
Ah, the audacity! Ah, the audacity of men: though Vishnu, Lord of the world, is present, the pride-swollen do not worship him.
Without worshipping the Lord of the world, Achyuta, the sustainer of all, how do those sunk in the ocean of samsara cross to the other shore?
By the medicine of uttering the names Achyuta, Ananta, Govinda, all diseases are destroyed; I speak true, true.
Those who always say "Narayana, Jagannatha, Vasudeva, Janardana" are honoured everywhere.
Even now Brahma and the other gods do not know his greatness; go to him for refuge, O sage.
Ah, the folly, the folly of the wicked: they do not know Vishnu abiding in the lotus of the heart, Narada.
Hear, tiger among sages, I say again and again: Hari is pleased with the faithful, not with wealth or kinsmen.
Kinsmen, wealth and sons come, O best one, to men devoted to Vishnu birth after birth.
This body has sin as its root and delights in sinful acts; knowing this, Janardana should be worshipped constantly.
Sons, friends, wives, and abundant wealth come, without doubt, to those devoted to worship of Hari.
One who wishes happiness here and hereafter should worship Hari constantly; one who wishes unhappiness here and hereafter should busy himself with slandering others.
Cursed is the birth of those without devotion to Janardana, God of gods; cursed again and again is wealth empty of gifts to worthy recipients.
The body that does not bow to Vishnu, the destroyer of karma's divisions, is to be known as a mine of sins, O best of sages.
Wealth that is without gifts to the worthy and guarded by someone — know it to be like what is guarded by theft, certainly, in the world.
Those intoxicated by wealth fickle as lightning, short-lived, do not worship the Lord of the universe, the liberator from the bonds of the bound.
Creation is declared twofold, divine and demonic; with devotion to Hari it is divine, without it greatly demonic.
Therefore hear, O best of Brahmins: those devoted to Hari are the best, famed everywhere, since devotion is exceedingly rare.
Keshava is pleased with those free of envy, devoted to protecting Brahmins, and free of desire and the like.
Those who delight in serving Vishnu by sweeping and so on, and in giving to worthy recipients, go to the highest place.
The ageless supreme eternal Brahman is known by knowledge alone; it is full, supreme bliss; therefore there is nothing else here, O Brahmin.
From sayings like "You are That," knowledge is the means of liberation; when knowledge is accomplished and unobstructed, all becomes Brahman.
Thus instructed by him, O lord of sages, Vedamali rejoiced, seeing the Lord Achyuta in the Self within the Self.
Brahman, free of limiting adjuncts, self-luminous, stainless — "I am that alone" — resolving so he attained supreme peace.
Then, for worldly conduct, Vedamali, bowing to his teacher, the lord of sages, always remained devoted to meditation.
After much time had passed, Vedamali, lord of sages, reached the city of Varanasi and attained supreme liberation.
He who reads or attentively hears this chapter cuts the bonds of karma and attains happiness.
Even tormented by the fire of hunger, he reached Hari's temple; then rain fell there and that place became muddy.
With the wish to stand there, you scraped away the mud; that place in Vishnu's temple became plastered.
Having reached nearness to Hari for a full hundred crores of kalpas, you will live there, gain knowledge, and go to supreme liberation.
You wish to uplift your younger brother, the foremost of sinners; we shall tell you the means; understand, great-minded one.
Give the fruit of plastering a space of a cow's-hide's measure of ground, and uplift your brother, O fortunate one, filled with mercy.
Thus told by Vishnu's messengers, the great man Yajnamali gave that fruit to his brother to free him from sin.
Sumali, freed of sin by the merit given by his brother, was left by Yama's messengers, who fled.
An aerial car with every enjoyment arrived at once; then Sumali mounted the heavenly vehicle and rejoiced, O sage.
Both brothers, O Brahmin, honoured by hosts of gods, embraced each other and gained great joy.
Yajnamali and Sumali, praised by great sages and sung by Gandharvas, went to Vishnu's world.
Having attained likeness to Hari's world, O best of sages, Sumali and Yajnamali lived there joyfully for one kalpa.
Having enjoyed many pleasures there, the great-minded Yajnamali, endowed with knowledge right there, attained supreme liberation.
Sumali, the fortunate, rejoiced in Vishnu's world; having stayed, he returned to earth and was born a Brahmin,
in a very pure family, virtuous and master of the Veda, endowed with every prosperity, devoted to Hari.
Uttering Hari's names, he went to the Ganga bank, bathed in the Ganga there, and saw the Lord Vishveshvara.
He attained the supreme state, hard to get even for yogis. Thus the greatness of plastering has been told to you, O lord of sages.
Therefore the Lord of the world should be worshipped with all effort; those who worship Vishnu even once, though unwillingly,
never have the bond of worldly existence. One who is devoted to Hari and worships with the thought of Hari,
Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara are pleased with him, O Brahmin. By mere association with companions devoted to Hari,
even one with great sins is freed from all sins. Of those devoted to worship of Hari and to his name,
those who serve them, even sinners, go to the highest state.

Ah, I of sinful mind constantly committed great sin. How can I have atonement? Whose refuge, O Lord, shall I go to?
naradapuran:36:56	By sins earned in a former birth I became a hunter; here too, having made nets of sin, what end shall I reach?
naradapuran:36:57	Ah, my life quickly wastes away; I have heaped up many sins and made no remedy for them. What will be my fate, or my birth?
naradapuran:36:58	Ah, Fate, why did you create me, a family of hundreds of sins, ever more sinful? How shall I, of terrible deeds, enjoy the fruit of sin in how many births?
Thus reviling himself, the hunter, burned by the fire of inner remorse, at once died.
Seeing the hunter fallen, Uttanka, wise and compassionate, sprinkled him with water from Vishnu's feet.
By the touch of water from Hari's feet the hunter, free of sin, boarded a heavenly aerial car and spoke to the sage:
Gulika said: "O Uttanka, tiger among sages, you are my teacher, O firm in vows; by your grace I am freed from the armour of great sins.
By your teaching my remorse has gone, O best of sages, and all sins have been destroyed very quickly.
Since you sprinkled water from Hari's feet on me, O sage, I have been brought by you to Vishnu's highest abode.
You have saved me, O Brahmin, from this sin and from this body; therefore I bow to you, O learned one; forgive what I did."
Having said so, he showered the best of sages with divine flowers, circumambulated him three times, and bowed.
Then, boarding the aerial car with every desire, surrounded by hosts of Apsarases, he reached Hari's temple.
Seeing this, Uttanka, the treasury of austerity, was astonished; placing his folded hands on his head, he praised the Lord of Lakshmi.
Praised by him, Mahavishnu gave him the best boon; by that boon Uttanka too attained the supreme state.
With a thousand heads, a thousand feet, a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, the primal one, delighted in by all sacrifices — I bow to the giver of satisfaction, of fierce valour.

Of the nature of Time, cause of the divisions of time, beyond the three qualities, knower of qualities, lover of qualities, giver of desires, free of attachment, beyond the senses, enjoyer of the world, free of thirst,
free of striving, foremost, unreachable even by mind, made of mind and made of food, firmly established, divided as understanding, of fixed order — I worship him who is not made of speech or breath.
Whose form, strength, power, deeds and measure the gods, Brahma and the rest do not know — how shall I praise him, the Self-form?

Fallen in the ocean of samsara, miserly, confused by delusion, bound by a hundred desires, infamous, slanderous, ungrateful, always impure, sunk in sin, very angry — O ocean of mercy, save me, terrified; again and again I take refuge in you.
Thus propitiated by him, the merciful Lord of Lakshmi, the treasury of splendour, became visible to him.
Flax-flower dark, with eyes like blossoming lotuses, crowned, with earrings, adorned with necklace and armlets,
bearing the Shrivatsa and Kaustubha, with a golden sacred thread, with a pearl set on his nose, his body radiance growing,
clothed in yellow, adorned with a garland of wild flowers, his feet worshipped with tender tulsi leaves, of great splendour,
shining with bells and anklets and the like, with the Garuda banner — seeing him, the best of Brahmins bowed like a staff on the earth.
Uttanka washed Hari's feet with tears of joy, crying "Murari, protect me, protect me!", with no other thought.
Raising him, the compassionate Mahavishnu embraced him and said to the best of sages: "Choose a boon, child."
There is nothing impossible to you when I am pleased, O best. Hearing this, Uttanka, bowing again to the God of gods, Janardana, the bearer of the discus, said:

Why do you bewilder me, Lord? What are other boons to me, O God? May my devotion to you be firm, birth after birth.
naradapuran:37:48	Whether I am born among worms, birds, beasts, reptiles, demons, ghouls or men — wherever, Keshava, by your grace let me have unshakable, unswerving devotion in you.
So be it, said the Lord of the world, and touching him with the tip of his conch, he gave him divine knowledge, hard to get even for yogis.
As he praised, the God of gods, Janardana, smiling, placed his hand on the Brahmin's head and said this:
The Lord said: "Always worship me with the yoga of action, O best of Brahmins. Go to the abode of Nara and Narayana, and you will go to liberation.
The man who constantly reads this hymn made by you will obtain all desires and at the end become a sharer in liberation."
Having said so, Madhava vanished right there, O sage; and Uttanka went from there to the abode of Nara-Narayana.
Why should devotion to the God of gods who bears the discus always be practised? Devotion to Hari is declared supreme, giving the fruit of all desires.
Uttanka, with devotion, devoted to the yoga of action, always worshipping Madhava in the hermitage of Nara and Narayana,
endowed with knowledge and realization, his doubts of duality cut, attained Vishnu's supreme abode, hard to attain.
Worshipped, bowed to, or remembered, Narayana, Lord of the world, grants liberation and increases the honour of his devotees.
Therefore the god Narayana, infinite and unconquered, should be worshipped with devotion by one wishing happiness here and hereafter.
He who attentively reads or hears this account is freed from all sins and goes to Hari's abode.
In the Vaivasvata age long ago, there was a great dialogue between Indra and Brihaspati; I shall tell it; listen.
Once Indra, rich in every enjoyment, surrounded by the gods and thronged by Apsarases, said to Brihaspati:
Indra said: "O Brihaspati of great fortune, knower of the meaning of all truths, what sort of creation was there, O lord, in the previous kalpa of Brahma?
What was Indra said to be like, what were the gods said to be, and what were their deeds? You ought to tell me truly."
Brihaspati said: "O Indra, I do not know the conduct of the Creator of the previous day; even the present day seems to me hard to know.
The Manus who have passed — I am not able to name them. I shall tell you now who knows it; listen.
There lives in your city one famed as Sudharma, enjoying divine pleasures, who came here from Brahma's world.
He knows this; I shall tell you of him; listen." Thus told by his teacher, Indra,
accompanied by Brihaspati and thronged by hosts of gods, went to Sudharma's dwelling.
Seeing the lord of the gods arrive with Brihaspati, O divine sage, Sudharma honoured him respectfully as was fitting.
Honoured by Sudharma, Indra, seeing his excellent splendour, was struck with wonder in mind and said humbly:
Indra said: "If you know the history of the previous kalpa of Brahma, O wise one, tell it; I have come with my teacher to ask this.
By what do you know the gods who have passed from sleep (i.e., from before), O firm in vows? Tell me: why are you superior even to us, living in heaven?
In splendour, fame, renown, knowledge, giving or austerity, how are you thus, O lord?" Thus addressed by the king of the gods, Sudharma laughed,
and humbly told the earlier history in due order. Sudharma said: "A thousand sets of four ages are called one day of Brahma. In one day, O Indra, there are fourteen Manus,
(a thousand sets of four ages are called one day of Brahma; in one day there are fourteen Manus),
fourteen Indras are declared, and various gods separately. Of all the Indras and the Manus and so on, O Vasava,
there is equality in splendour, prosperity, power and strength. I shall tell their names; hear attentively.
First Svayambhuva Manu, then Svarochisha, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata and Chakshusha;
Vaivasvata Manu, the eighth Surya-savarni, the ninth Daksha-savarni, devoted to the good of all gods;
the tenth Brahma-savarni, then Dharma-savarni, then Rudra-savarni, then Rochamana;
and the fourteenth is called Bhautya. These are the Manus. Now I shall tell the gods and Indras; hear, O best of gods.
In Svayambhuva's period the gods are called Yamas; Shachipati is the great lord, their Indra.
In Svarochisha's period, the gods are the Paravatas and Tushitas; the lord of gods named Vipashchit, endowed with all prosperity.
The Sudhamans, Satyas, Shivas and others; their Indra is Sushanti, declared for the third.
The Suras, Paraharas, Sutyas and Asudhis; their Indra is called Shiva, Shakra, in the Tamasa period; the fifth is the lord of gods named Vibhu.
Hear now of the sixth: the Amitabhas and others; the Aryas and others are declared gods, their Indra is Manojava.
In the Vaivasvata period the gods are the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras and others; Indra is called Purandara, endowed with every desire.
The immeasurable gods, Sutapas and others are declared; by the power of worship of Vishnu, their Indra is Bali.
In the ninth the gods are the Parads and others, and Indra is called Adbhuta; in the tenth the gods are Suvasanas and others.
Their Indra is Shanti, endowed with all enjoyments; the gods are Vihangamas and others, their Indra is Vrisha.
In the eleventh and twelfth, hear what I shall tell: Indra named Ritadhama, the gods are the Haritas.
In the thirteenth period the gods are Sutramas and others; Divaspati, of great valour, is declared their Indra.
In the fourteenth the gods are the Chakshusas and others; Indra is Shuchi. Thus the Manus, Indras and gods have been told in truth.
In one day of Brahma they exercise their own offices.
In all creations in the worlds, the creation is held to be of one kind; there are many creators, and only the expert knows their number.
While I have been in Brahma's world, many Brahmas have gone; I am not able to count them today, O best of Brahmins.
Hear how long I stayed even after reaching the world of heaven: four Manus have passed; my prosperity is very great.
I must stay here for a hundred crore of ages, O lord; then I shall go to the world of action; hear it from me.
I shall tell you the deed I did before, O firm in vows — destroying all sins for those who speak and hear it.
Formerly, O Indra, I was a vulture, especially sinful, living in a part of the earth and eating impure flesh.
Once I was perched on the wall of Vishnu's temple, O lord, and fell, struck by a hunter's weapon, in the temple courtyard at evening.
As my life was at my throat, a fierce dog greedy for flesh seized me in its mouth, and ran with other dogs.
Carrying me in its mouth, afraid of the other dogs, it went round Vishnu's temple in circumambulation, O lord.
By that alone the Inner Self of the world was pleased and gave both me and the dog the highest state.
Such a fruit was gained, O best of gods, even by going in circumambulation; what then of proper worship?"
Thus told by the great Sudharma, the king of gods was pleased in mind and became devoted to worship of Hari.
Even so, all the immortals wish to be born in Bharata and worship the Lord of gods, Narayana, the faultless; Brahma and the hosts of gods constantly worship them.
For great souls intent on remembering Narayana, who have abandoned possessions, how can there be bondage to fierce worldly existence, if they are greedy for his company and partake of liberation?
Men who daily worship Narayana, whose vehicle is Garuda, free of attachment, are freed on all sides from heaps of sins and go gladly to Vishnu's highest abode.
Men who, free of passion, knowing the higher and lower, constantly remember Narayana, teacher of the gods, by that meditation their sins are destroyed and they do not drink their mother's milk again.
Men faultless in hearing Hari's stories and devoted to worship of Krishna's lotus feet purify even the worlds by contact of body; by merely speaking with them too, Hari is worshipped.
Where there are great ones devoted to worship of Hari with pure minds, there all good is, as water flows to low ground, O Brahmin.
